measured_failure: Prior corrected pulse angular/joint-velocity one-step residual is 0.687720 rad/s despite initial force-row feasibility. The predictor uses initial executable torque for 20 ms; the plant executes a position/velocity/feedforward command throughout the interval.
prerequisite: Separate command realization and integration error from a physical-parameter mismatch before identifying friction, compliance or actuator lag.
hypothesis: Evaluating the known servo command along predicted states reduces angular/joint-velocity residual by at least 10 percent relative to 2 ms frozen-torque integration on both nominal selection data and the separate pulse condition.
variants: Frozen initial torque, one 20 ms step
Frozen initial torque, ten 2 ms predictor steps
Issued servo law evaluated at predicted states, ten 2 ms predictor steps
selection: Archived corrected nominal estimated transitions starting at 4.00 through 5.98 s; no physical parameter fitted.
reserved: Archived corrected pulse estimated transitions starting at 4.50 through 5.98 s; excluded from selection.
additional_measurement: Evaluate the previous command at the next estimated state before changing commands. Count loss of model cone feasibility despite feasible initial rows. This uses observed endpoints for scoring only.
controller_inputs: Only archived estimated states and issued commands. No future observations enter predictor trajectories. Known command gains and controller torque limits are retained.
hardware_ranges: None selected. Existing synthetic 10 mm/0.01 rad base bias and ideal joint/velocity channels are unmeasured hardware assumptions.
decision_rule: A failed command-model or between-command feasibility prerequisite completes this prerequisite question with measured limitations; do not attribute its residual to an identified physical parameter or report closed-loop adaptation benefit. A successful predictor alone also does not establish closed-loop benefit.
